assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell reframed intracellular organization as a physical-chemistry problem of phase behaviour, multivalent interactions and thermodynamics. It established a new concept of molecular organisation (membraneless condensates, P granules, nucleoli) with broad reach into cell biology, neurodegeneration and materials-like protein assemblies.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed liquid-like P granules in 2009; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work (2012) gave the quantitative, chemically defined framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence-encoded theory and IDR grammar, so the three-person limit leaves real allocation tension.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is wide and independent, and the concept is firmly established. Debate remains about which in-cell condensates are truly equilibrium phases, so timing is good but the interpretation is still being refined.
uncertainties: Controversy over physiological relevance of in-vitro droplets versus in-cell condensates
Credit split between cell-biological discovery, multivalency theory and sequence-grammar work
Possible fit to Chemistry versus Physiology or Medicine

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly applied to deliver nucleic acids, and they enabled the mRNA COVID-19 vaccines and siRNA therapeutics. It is an engineering of lipid phase behaviour, pKa-dependent charge and membrane fusion with enormous demonstrated societal impact.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) established the lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable-lipid delivery principles; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid libraries and delivery concepts, MacLachlan the clinical translation. Credit is plausible for a trio but contested at the margins and overlaps with the 2023 mRNA prize.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is overwhelming and independent. Timing is ripe, though the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modifications may be seen as having partly covered the topic.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA
Whether Cullis-group work or later ionizable-lipid optimization is decisive
Industrial versus academic credit and patent disputes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory turned protein folding into a statistical-mechanical problem of free-energy surfaces, frustration and hydrophobic driving forces, resolving Levinthal's paradox conceptually. It is the kind of general physical-chemical principle reducing a complex biological process to thermodynamics that I value.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill are the central theorists of landscape and funnel ideas; Bryngelson and Fersht provided the early formulation and experimental phi-value mapping. The trio is defensible but Fersht's experimental contribution is left out.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental and computational support, including links to AlphaFold-era structure prediction, though the latter is a different advance. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Distinction from the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design
Fersht and Bryngelson credit left out
Concept is partly theoretical rather than a single discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues created a new pharmacological modality, re-explaining thalidomide-class drugs through cereblon and enabling destruction of formerly undruggable proteins. Strong chemical-biology concept, now in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001); Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target; Ciulli, Gray and others advanced VHL and degrader design. Credit is spread over concept, target identification and chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Several degraders are in late-stage trials but no approved PROTAC drug yet. Impact is large, though the validation is still maturing.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet
Allocation between PROTAC inventors and the thalidomide-mechanism discoverers
Fit between Chemistry and Medicine

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers on gold and related surfaces are a clean example of molecular organisation at interfaces, governed by surface energetics and intermolecular forces, and underpin soft lithography, surface functionalization and biosensing. They fit my interest in interfaces and colloid chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported alkanethiolate/disulfide monolayers on gold (1983); Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers have priority claims; Whitesides developed the broad applications and soft lithography. Priority and attribution are mixed, with Sagiv and Xia complicating the trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed for decades, so recognition is timely or somewhat late, with a risk that it is seen as a methodology rather than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Sagiv priority on silane monolayers
Whether the prize would cover SAMs, soft lithography or both
Impact seen as enabling methodology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules showed that coordination thermodynamics can encode complex three-dimensional architectures with defined cavities, giving host-guest chemistry, confined catalysis and molecular recognition. A general self-assembly concept with durable impact.
assessment.attribution: Fujita (square and cage assemblies, 1990), Stang (molecular architecture via coordination-driven assembly) and Raymond (tetrahedral and other cages, catalysis in cavities) are decisive contributors; Nitschke and Ward are important later developers. A three-person split is feasible.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over three decades. Supramolecular chemistry was recognized in 1987 and 2016, so some may regard this as an extension.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier supramolecular and mechanically interlocked prizes
Real-world application is less demonstrated than the concept
Precise allocation among Fujita, Stang and Raymond

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a fast rise in solar-cell efficiency from about 4 percent to over 25 percent and are a defect-tolerant semiconductor family of general materials-chemistry interest. The scientific and energy relevance is high.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell (2009); Park's solid-state cell (2012) and Snaith's meso-superstructured cells and Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok all contributed decisively. Allocation is difficult with six credited names.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency gains are reproducible, but long-term stability and commercialization are not yet settled, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Operational stability and lead toxicity unresolved
Complex credit among six or more contributors
May be better aligned with Physics

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a general platform for radical chemistry, using photoexcited catalysts to drive single-electron transfer in mild organic synthesis, with wide adoption in pharmaceutical chemistry. A clear concept with large practical reach.
assessment.attribution: MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson independently reported the 2008 foundational papers, while Fukuzumi, Konig, Nicewicz and Melchiorre made related and later contributions. Credit is plausible for these three but MacMillan is already a laureate (2021).
assessment.maturity: Heavily validated and widely applied, so timely, though MacMillan's 2021 prize may reduce urgency and some see it as a method.
uncertainties: MacMillan already honoured in 2021
Priority questions relative to earlier photoinduced electron-transfer work
Physical-chemistry grounding is weaker than for other candidates
